papers.abstract_en: AIMS: First-line chemoimmunotherapy (ICI-chemo) has become the standard of care for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). However, older adults are underrepresented in pivotal trials due to strict inclusion criteria that limit participation to highly selected, fit patients. Given the limited real-world comparative data, this study aimed to determine whether older adults with ES-SCLC derive greater benefit from ICI-chemo compared with chemotherapy (chemo) alone. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study including ES-SCLC patients aged 65 years or older who started first-line ICI-chemo or chemo between January 2020 and July 2024. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to adjust for baseline confounding. The main outcome was overall survival (OS) in the IPTW population. RESULTS: In the IPTW population, median OS was significantly longer in the ICI-chemo group (14.95 months; 95% CI, 12.94-19.91) compared with chemo (10.28 months; 95% CI, 8.11-13.17; HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.48-0.91; p = 0.011). Multivariable analysis confirmed that ICI-chemo exposure was independently associated with improved OS (HR, 0.608; 95% CI, 0.440-0.841; p = 0.003). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide comparative evidence of improved survival in association with ICI-chemo compared with chemo in older adults with ES-SCLC.

papers.abstract_en: The application of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has reshaped the perioperative treatment pattern of resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Currently, three treatment paradigms have emerged: adjuvant, neoadjuvant alone, and 'sandwich' (neoadjuvant+surgery+adjuvant). Although IMpower010 and KEYNOTE-091 achieved positive results in adjuvant immunotherapy, the negative results of two large phase III studies, BR.31 and ANVIL, raised questions about the generalizability of this model. In contrast, neoadjuvant immunotherapy has shown efficacy in multiple phase III studies. This advantage may stem from the preservation of the intact tumor antigen repertoire and draining lymph node architecture, enabling chemo-immunotherapy to elicit more robust systemic immune responses. Currently, both neoadjuvant alone and 'sandwich' models are recommended by guidelines, but the 5-year overall survival (OS) rates of CheckMate-816 and KEYNOTE-671 are nearly identical (65.4% vs 64.6%), and the pathological complete response (pCR) rate of CheckMate-77T (25.3%) is comparable to that of CheckMate-816 (24%), suggesting that the incremental benefit of extending neoadjuvant cycles and adding postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy in the 'sandwich' model is very limited. In the future, an individualized decision-making model based on pCR and molecular residual disease (MRD) status, such as de-escalation to observation for those achieving pCR with negative MRD, and intensification for those with residual disease or positive MRD, is expected to optimize the balance between treatment intensity and survival benefit. In summary, the existing evidence favors the adoption of a 'neoadjuvant first' strategy for resectable NSCLC. Based mainly on cross-trial indirect comparisons, the neoadjuvant alone model offers comparable efficacy to the 'sandwich' approach with potential cost-effectiveness advantages, and may be preferred as the initial strategy. Individualized post-neoadjuvant management represents the future direction of this field. .

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Vibostolimab, an anti-T-cell immunoreceptor with immunoglobulin and ITIM domains (TIGIT) antibody, showed antitumor activity with pembrolizumab in non-small-cell lung cancer. OBJECTIVE: The KEYVIBE-008 study evaluated vibostolimab coformulated with pembrolizumab (vibostolimab/pembrolizumab) plus etoposide and platinum-based chemotherapy (EP) versus atezolizumab plus EP as first-line therapy for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. METHODS: Participants aged ≥18 years with untreated extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer were randomized 1:1 to vibostolimab/pembrolizumab (200 mg each) or atezolizumab (1200 mg) every 3 weeks, with EP and cisplatin/carboplatin for the first four cycles. The primary endpoint was overall survival. The prespecified interim analysis included a non-binding futility analysis of overall survival (futility threshold for actual number of events, P = 0.4816). RESULTS: Four hundred and sixty participants were randomized (both arms, n = 230). Median time from randomization to data cutoff (4 June, 2024) was 16.6 (range 11.3‒26.1) months. The prespecified futility criterion for overall survival was met (hazard ratio 1.26; 95% confidence interval 1.00‒1.59; P = 0.9762). There was no difference in progression-free survival (hazard ratio 1.01; 95% confidence interval 0.82‒1.23) or objective response rates (71.7% with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab vs 74.8% with atezolizumab). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 66.8% of participants treated with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab and 57.2% treated with atezolizumab. Immune-mediated adverse events and infusion reactions occurred in 39.3% and 29.7% of participants, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In this interim analysis of vibostolimab/pembrolizumab plus EP versus atezolizumab plus EP as first-line therapy for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer, the prespecified futility criterion for overall survival was met. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events and immune-mediated adverse events were more frequent with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab versus atezolizumab. Given the overall benefit/risk profile, treatment with vibostolimab/pembrolizumab was discontinued. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov, NCT05224141.

papers.abstract_en: Hypoxia-driven epigenetic remodeling is a critical determinant of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epigenetic mechanisms coordinating hypoxia signaling with tumor microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood. Here, by integrating LUAD cell models, murine tumor models, and spatial transcriptomics with reference-based cell-type deconvolution, we identify SATB2 as a previously unrecognized hypoxia-inducible epigenetic regulator in LUAD. HIF-1α, unlike HIF-2α, directly interacts with the promoter of SATB2, promoting its expression in hypoxic environments. Increased levels of SATB2 have been linked to more severe clinical and pathological characteristics as well as poorer outcomes for patients. Mechanistically, SATB2 physically interacts with HIF-1α and p300, while SATB2 loss reduces H3K27 acetylation and elongating RNA polymerase II occupancy at HIF-1 target loci, supporting a model in which SATB2 facilitates HIF-1α-dependent transcriptional elongation and establishes a positive feedback circuit that amplifies hypoxia-responsive transcriptional programs. Spatial transcriptomic analyses further show that SATB2-associated hypoxic programs are preferentially enriched within malignant tumor niches and are associated with remodeling of the local tumor microenvironment. Functionally, SATB2 promotes LUAD growth, metastasis, angiogenesis, and bevacizumab resistance in a HIF-1α-dependent manner, whereas genetic disruption of SATB2 or pharmacological inhibition of p300 enhances sensitivity to anti-angiogenic therapy. Collectively, these findings identify the SATB2-p300-HIF-1α axis as a hypoxia-responsive epigenetic regulatory mechanism linking transcriptional adaptation to malignant progression and resistance to anti-angiogenic therapy, and provide a preclinical rationale for further investigation of this pathway as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: World Trade Center (WTC)-exposed Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) rescue/recovery workers have an elevated risk of smoking-related morbidity. Despite access to free tobacco cessation treatment, some individuals in this population continue to smoke. In other settings, opt-out treatment approaches increase treatment initiation, but effectiveness in occupational health programs is unclear. Accordingly, we (1) assessed whether an opt-out strategy increases engagement with a Tobacco Cessation Program and (2) identified factors associated with engagement. METHODS: This was a randomized trial among FDNY firefighters and Emergency Medical Service (EMS) who self-reported smoking and were eligible for the WTC Health Program Lung Cancer Screening Program. 1:1 randomization occurred prior to contact for opt-out recruitment with Enhanced Care treatment (Opt-Out/Enhanced) or opt-in recruitment with Standard Care treatment (Opt-In/Standard). Opt-Out/Enhanced included proactive outreach and tailored biofeedback during counseling; Opt-In/Standard included participant-initiated engagement and standard counseling. Both groups were offered identical no-cost pharmacotherapy (varenicline). Engagement was defined as: consented enrollment (expressed interest and provided informed consent) and treatment initiation (attendance at ≥1 counseling session). Engagement differences were evaluated using logistic regression; sociodemographic and health-related factors were characterized descriptively without formal testing due to small numbers. RESULTS: Overall, 312 individuals were randomized (Opt-Out/Enhanced, n = 156 and Opt-In/Standard, n = 156). Engagement was low (7.4%). Consented enrollment (n = 23; OR = 3.05; 95% CI = 1.11-9.72) and treatment initiation (n = 18; OR = 2.08; 95% CI = 0.72-6.73) were higher in Opt-Out/Enhanced versus Opt-In/Standard. Treatment initiators had a median age of 60.5 (vs 65.0 years among non-initiators); 38.9% were EMS (vs 18.0%), 22.2% were female (vs 6.9%), 77.8% had a prior cessation attempt (vs 23.5%), and 55.6% had abnormal lung function (vs 32.9%). Participants were too few to analyze cessation outcomes in depth. CONCLUSIONS: Despite low engagement overall, opt-out treatment had higher engagement with tobacco cessation treatment. This supports other work that has found opt-out treatment to be encouraged for hard-to-reach populations.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Lung resection is the standard curative treatment for resectable lung cancer; however, postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) and prolonged hospital length of stay (LOS) remain major barriers to recovery and healthcare efficiency. Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) and prehabilitation are distinct perioperative strategies that differ in their timing, intervention components, and mechanisms of action, but both aim to optimize patients' perioperative condition and improve postoperative recovery. However, their effectiveness compared with conventional perioperative care based solely on randomized controlled trials (RCTs) has not been comprehensively synthesized. OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of ERAS and prehabilitation in reducing PPCs, shortening LOS, and improving patient-reported outcomes following pulmonary resection for lung cancer. SUBJECTS AND METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs involving adults undergoing pulmonary resection for primary lung cancer. Searches of PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, CINAHL Complete, RISS, KISS, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform identified studies published between January 2015 and May 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled odds ratios (ORs) for PPCs and mean differences (MDs) for LOS. Patient-reported outcomes were synthesized narratively according to the SWiM guideline. RESULTS: Ten RCTs involving 1,569 participants met the inclusion criteria. ERAS and prehabilitation significantly reduced PPCs compared with conventional perioperative care (OR = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.36-0.65, p < 0.001). The exploratory pooled analysis suggested a shorter postoperative LOS (MD = -2.30 days, 95% CI = -3.58 to -1.01); however, heterogeneity was considerable (I 2 = 97.9%), and the 95% prediction interval crossed the null. Narrative synthesis demonstrated consistent improvements in anxiety, depression, postoperative pain, pulmonary function, quality of life, and functional recovery. CONCLUSION: ERAS and prehabilitation are effective perioperative strategies for improving outcomes after pulmonary resection for lung cancer. Their implementation in routine clinical practice may reduce postoperative complications, accelerate recovery, and improve healthcare efficiency. Further multicenter RCTs are needed to optimize intervention components, standardize outcome measures, and strengthen evidence for long-term and patient-reported outcomes. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: CRD420261373242.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dexmedetomidine has increasingly been incorporated into opioid-sparing anesthetic strategies during video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) because of its analgesic properties and minimal respiratory depression. However, dexmedetomidine remains associated with dose-related hemodynamic adverse effects, particularly bradycardia and hypotension. We evaluated whether a reduced-dose dexmedetomidine regimen decreases intraoperative opioid requirements while maintaining acceptable hemodynamic safety during VATS. METHODS: In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 68 patients undergoing VATS were randomly assigned to either a dexmedetomidine group or a control group (34 patients each). The dexmedetomidine group received a loading dose of 0.5 µg/kg followed by continuous infusion at 0.5 µg/kg/h during surgery. The control group received conventional fentanyl-based anesthesia. The primary outcome was maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl consumption. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), postoperative respiratory complications, and perioperative safety outcomes. RESULTS: Maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl consumption was significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (18.7 vs. 33.2 µg, P = 0.009). Postoperative pain scores, rescue analgesic requirements, PONV, and respiratory complications were comparable between groups. However, the dexmedetomidine group demonstrated a higher incidence of intraoperative bradycardia (23.5% vs. 0%, P = 0.005) and postoperative hypotension during PACU stay (23.5% vs. 2.9%, P = 0.027). These hemodynamic events were transient and responsive to pharmacologic intervention. CONCLUSIONS: Dexmedetomidine-based opioid-sparing anesthesia reduced maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl administration during VATS. However, the reduction was modest, was not associated with clear postoperative benefits, and was accompanied by increased bradycardia and hypotension. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05431322), registered on 14 June 2022. Available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05431322 .

papers.abstract_en: Dysregulated splicing factors play critical roles in tumor progression. Here, we identify family with sequence similarity 50 member A (FAM50A) as a pivotal oncogenic splicing factor involved in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Multi-omics and multi-cohort analyses revealed that FAM50A is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with a poor prognosis. Functional studies demonstrated that FAM50A promotes ESCC proliferation and migration both in vitro and in vivo, primarily through the activation of mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs) and focal adhesion kinase (FAK). We further characterized the FAM50A-binding RNA motif and established its transcriptome-wide splicing landscape. Notably, we identified a novel FAM50A-dependent backsplicing event that generates circSDK1, which originates from exons 2-4 of the sidekick cell adhesion molecule 1 (SDK1) pre-mRNA. Mechanistically, circSDK1 binds to dual-specificity phosphatase 22 (DUSP22) and occupies its phosphatase domain, inhibiting the DUSP22-mediated dephosphorylation of MAPKs and FAK and thereby sustaining their activation. Furthermore, the transcription factor TFAP2C increased FAM50A expression. Finally, we identified rifabutin as a small-molecule inhibitor of FAM50A and confirmed its anti-tumor efficacy in cell-derived xenograft, patient-derived organoid, and patient-derived xenograft models. In summary, FAM50A promotes ESCC progression via the FAM50A/circSDK1/DUSP22 axis, leading to MAPKs and FAK activation. Genetic or pharmacological targeting of FAM50A with rifabutin represents a promising therapeutic strategy for ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bronchiectasis in women of reproductive age is increasingly recognized, yet data on fertility and pregnancy outcomes remain limited. RESEARCH QUESTION: What are fertility characteristics, pregnancy outcomes, and patient-reported reproductive health experiences in women with bronchiectasis? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study across EMBARC-affiliated centers including women with bronchiectasis and pregnancy between 2012 and 2023. Clinical, pulmonary, obstetric, and neonatal data were collected. In parallel, an international patient survey assessed fertility, pregnancy, and hormonal influences on disease. Statistical analyses included comparative and correlation testing. RESULTS: Eighty-three women contributed data from 121 pregnancies and 123 neonates. Mean age at conception was 29.5 years. Assisted reproductive technologies were used in 32.1% of pregnancies, more frequently in primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) than other etiologies (48.5% vs. 8.7%, P=0.004). Lung function remained stable during and after pregnancy. Exacerbations occurred in 58.6% of pregnancies. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks and mean birth weight was 2.99 kg. Pre-pregnancy FEV1 correlated with birth weight (ρ=0.42, P=0.001) and gestational age (ρ=0.25, P=0.042). Neonatal outcomes were generally favorable. Survey data (n=629) demonstrated an early onset of menopause in women with bronchiectasis diagnosed before age 50 years compared to after 50 years. Women with PCD reported difficulties conceiving more often than women with early onset bronchiectasis without PCD. INTERPRETATION: Pregnancy in women with bronchiectasis is frequently complicated by exacerbations and low neonatal birth weight. Subfertility is primarily driven by PCD, while non-PCD bronchiectasis shows rates similar to the general population. Pre-pregnancy lung function is associated with neonatal outcomes, supporting the importance of pulmonary optimization and multidisciplinary care before and during pregnancy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung transplantation is a feasible therapeutic option for irreversible lung injury caused by COVID-19, but comprehensive mid-term outcome data remain limited. This study evaluated outcomes after lung transplantation for COVID-19 acute respiratory distress syndrome (CARDS) and post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis (CPF) using a national registry. METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of the United Network for Organ Sharing database from 2020 through 2024. Recipient characteristics, perioperative complications, and graft failure-free survival were analyzed in adult lung transplant recipients with a primary diagnosis of CARDS, CPF, or non-COVID restrictive lung disease (NCRLD). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and multivariate logistic regression were performed to adjust for potential confounders. RESULTS: During the study period, 256 transplants were performed for CARDS, 338 for CPF, and 8071 for NCRLD. Post-COVID-19 recipients were younger (54 vs. 64 years, p<0.001) and required a higher level of care preoperatively than NCRLD recipients. Posttransplant, post-COVID-19 recipients experienced higher rates of posttransplant ECMO (22.6% vs. 10.3%, p<0.001), ventilation >48 hours (67.5% vs. 43.3%, p<0.001), new dialysis (11.0% vs. 7.9%, p=0.012), and acute rejection (7.7% vs. 5.5%, p=0.026). Graft failure-free survival was equivalent throughout the first year posttransplant between the post-COVID-19 and NCRLD recipients and, after IPTW for age and other confounders, was equivalent for up to 3 years (Hochberg-adjusted p=0.118). CONCLUSIONS: Lung transplantation for post-COVID-19 lung damage yields comparable short-term and mid-term survival outcomes despite higher perioperative morbidity and resource utilization. Long-term studies are needed to assess chronic lung allograft dysfunction in this population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Whether lifetime lung function trajectories and spirometry patterns are associated with Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA) is unknown. We aimed to investigate this association to widen the understanding of OSA pathophysiology. METHODS: We previously identified six FEV1/FVC (forced expiratory volume in the first second/forced vital capacity) and five FVC trajectories within a population-based prospective cohort (n = 2422) using spirometry assessed at ages 7, 13, 18, 43, 50, and 53 years. These trajectories were combined into four lifetime spirometry patterns: restrictive-only, obstructive-only, mixed, and reference (normal), which were our exposure variables. Outcomes were medically-confirmed OSA in midlife and probable-OSA defined using the STOP-Bang questionnaire. Associations were assessed using logistic regression models. RESULTS: The 'restrictive-only' spirometry pattern was associated with medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 2.5; 95% CI 1.5, 4.3). In addition, restriction-confirmatory low total lung capacity and reduced functional residual capacity were associated with increased odds of medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 1.4; 0.9, 2.1 and OR = 1.7; 1.1, 2.6, respectively, per one SD reduction in volume). The results were similar for probable OSA. These associations held when controlled for BMI and central obesity and were independent of childhood lung function. Neither transfer factor for carbon monoxide (TLco) nor transfer coefficient (Kco) was associated with OSA. CONCLUSION: We provide first evidence that lifetime lung restriction is related to middle-age OSA. While this information may be used to incidentally flag middle-age OSA risk and vice versa, further research is encouraged to confirm the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal cancer (EC) is a highly prevalent and aggressive gastrointestinal malignancy. Late diagnosis and heterogeneous responses to chemoradiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapies severely challenge clinical management. Accumulating evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis influences esophageal mucosal malignant transformation, tumor progression, and therapeutic outcomes through the gut-esophageal axis. However, most existing research remains correlational. To bridge this gap, this review critically synthesizes the dysbiosis signatures of EC and establishes a five-tier evidence grading framework to rigorously distinguish causal mechanisms from preclinical inferences. This microbial regulation is predominantly driven by metabolite-mediated signaling, remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment (TME), intestinal barrier disruption, and oncogenic pathway activation. We functionally classify EC-associated dysbiosis into pro-tumorigenic, anti-tumorigenic, and context-dependent taxa, emphasizing a multidimensional ecosystem perspective. Furthermore, we evaluate the utility of gut microbial signatures as predictive biomarkers for neoadjuvant therapy and prognosis. Microbiota-targeted intervention strategies, including fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), microecological preparations, and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), have entered clinical exploration as adjunctive approaches to optimize treatment efficacy. Finally, we address current translational barriers and propose future directions, emphasizing multi-omics integration, spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI). This provides an objective, mechanistically grounded framework for advancing microbiota-guided personalized oncology in EC.

papers.abstract_en: Introduction Respiratory muscle impairment is common in patients with severe emphysema, primarily driven by lung hyperinflation. Endobronchial valve (EBV) treatment reduces hyperinflation and may restore respiratory mechanics in this patient population. Our aim was to investigate changes in neural drive and respiratory muscle recruitment following EBV treatment. Methods EBV-eligible emphysema patients from our prior study on diaphragm function were prospectively enrolled (NCT04735731). Respiratory muscle activation and timing were assessed using surface electromyography at baseline and 6 weeks following EBV treatment. Additionally, an age-matched control group without respiratory symptoms was included for comparison. Results We included 25 patients who underwent EBV treatment (mean FEV1 28% predicted, mean RV 233% predicted) and 12 controls. The inspiratory time (Ti) to total time of respiratory cycle (Ttot) ratio (0.35 vs 0.53; p=0.003) was significantly lower in patients compared to controls. Activity of the diaphragm (4.7 vs 0.9 µV; p<0.001) and intercostal muscles (1.2 vs 0.4 µV; p<0.001) during tidal breathing was significantly higher in patients. Furthermore, tonic (end-expiratory) activity of the diaphragm (1.4 vs 0.6 µV; p=0.012) and intercostal muscles (1.4 vs 0.6 µV; p=0.003) was significantly higher as well. Following EBV treatment, all measured outcomes improved significantly, approaching the values observed in the control group. Conclusion These findings indicate that neural drive and respiratory muscle effort are significantly elevated in severe emphysema patients. By reducing lung hyperinflation, endobronchial valve treatment reduces this load, resulting in improved respiratory mechanics and decreased work of breathing, an important contributor to dyspnoea severity.

papers.abstract_en: Bone metastasis of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) directly leads to poor prognosis. This study aimed to dissect the stromal landscape of LUAD with bone metastases. Unsupervised clustering of scRNA-seq data from LUAD patients with bone metastasis identifies stromal subsets. Pseudotime analysis combined with CytoTRACE stemness scoring reconstructs mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) differentiation trajectories, while CellChat characterizes cell-cell communication networks among MSC subpopulations. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) specific to functionally distinct MSC subsets are subjected to LASSO-Cox regression for construction of a prognostic RiskScore model, which is validated in independent bulk RNA-seq cohorts regarding overall survival, immune cell infiltration, and drug sensitivity. A distinct high-stemness MSC C1 subpopulation is localized at the bifurcation point of two divergent differentiation trajectories toward a matrix-remodeling fate and a secretory, immunomodulatory phenotype. The RiskScore model stratifies patients into low- and high-risk groups with divergent overall-survival outcomes. Reduced infiltration of cytotoxic lymphocytes is observed in high-risk patients, and higher drug sensitivity within the high-risk subgroup. In vitro assays verify that LDHA knockdown impairs proliferation and migration in A549 cells. This study provides a rationale for targeting stroma-derived genes in risk-adapted therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the malignant tumor with the highest incidence and mortality rates worldwide, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for approximately 85% of cases. Radical surgical resection serves as the primary curative modality for patients with resectable NSCLC; however, postoperative recurrence persists in a subset of patients, thereby compromising long-term survival outcomes. Consequently, the precise prediction of postoperative recurrence risk, identification of high-risk populations, and formulation of individualized adjuvant therapy and surveillance strategies are of paramount importance for improving patient prognosis. In recent years, fueled by the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) and liquid biopsy technologies, the prediction of postoperative recurrence in NSCLC has progressively transitioned toward greater precision and personalization. This review summarizes the current applications of traditional predictive models, AI-based models, and liquid biopsy techniques in forecasting NSCLC recurrence following surgery, evaluating their respective strengths and limitations. Furthermore, it provides insights into future research trajectories. .

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Despite strong evidence supporting perioperative pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) for patients undergoing lung cancer surgery, little is known about factors that may influence implementation prior to program rollout, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Guided by the updated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR 2.0), this study aimed to identify anticipated barriers and facilitators to inform program refinement and future implementation strategies. METHODS: A descriptive qualitative design was used. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nurses from the thoracic surgery department of a tertiary hospital in China (September-November 2025). Guided by the four CFIR 2.0 domains (innovation, outer setting, inner setting, individuals), directed content analysis was performed based on nurses' perspectives. RESULTS: Sixteen nurses were interviewed, representing diverse roles: Ward/ICU frontline staff nurses, charge nurses, unit secretaries, administrative nurses and nurse managers. Relevant constructs included 22 of the 29 CFIR 2.0 constructs and 8 subconstructs. Facilitators spanned: innovation (source, evidence base, relative advantage, trialability); outer setting (financing, policy, external pressure); inner setting (relational connections, communication, culture, incentive systems); and individual factors (team needs, leadership/practitioner capability, motivation). Barriers comprised: innovation (adaptability, complexity, cost); outer setting (local condition, partnerships and connections); inner setting (structural characteristics, compatibility, access to knowledge and information); and individuals (recipient needs, capability). Notably, implementation concerns differed across nursing roles, reflecting role heterogeneity and underscoring the need for tailored implementation strategies. CONCLUSION: Implementation of perioperative PR for patients undergoing lung cancer surgery is influenced by multilevel factors spanning innovation, outer setting, inner setting, and individuals determinants. Differences in concerns across nursing roles highlight the importance of role-tailored implementation strategies. These findings provide a foundation for optimizing implementation approaches and may facilitate the sustainable integration of evidence-based PR into routine practice, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare settings.

papers.abstract_en: Squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) comprise a group of lethal malignancies, yet developing SCC-specific therapies remains challenging, largely due to a lack of druggable targets. We identify SOX2 condensation as a shared cancer hallmark across esophageal, head and neck, and lung SCCs. Within SOX2, the activation domain 1 (AD1) acts as the condensate-promoting region via its aromatic and hydrophobic residues. Site-specific mutagenesis, orthotopic mouse models, and multi-omics sequencing demonstrate that SOX2 condensates upregulate oncogene expression by enhancing SOX2 chromatin occupancy, H3K27ac enrichment, and chromatin interactions at oncogenic loci such as FGFR2, thereby promoting SCC progression. An FDA-approved drug screen reveals that the proteasome inhibitor ixazomib disrupts SOX2 condensates in an HSP70-dependent manner. Upon ixazomib treatment, the substrate-binding domain of HSP70 blocks SOX2 AD1, selectively dissolving SOX2 condensates, downregulating oncogene expression, and suppressing condensate-positive SCC patient-derived xenografts. These findings highlight targeting SOX2 condensates with proteasome inhibitors as an SCC-specific, biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is among the most devastating modes of progression in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although dose escalation of third-generation EGFR-TKIs has been an important central nervous system (CNS)-directed salvage strategy, therapeutic options after progression on this intensification approach remain limited. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients treated between September 2024 and December 2025. Eligible patients were adults (≥18 years) with histologically confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, a documented EGFR mutation, and LM diagnosed by gadolinium-enhanced MRI or positive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology. Patients received ivonescimab plus chemotherapy after documented intracranial or extracranial progression on a dose-escalated third-generation EGFR-TKI regimen used for LM management, with or without concurrent CSF-directed therapy. Ivonescimab was given intravenously at 20 mg/kg every 3 weeks with chemotherapy selected according to prior treatment and clinical status. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and LM progression-free survival (LM-PFS). RESULTS: Of 517 screened patients, 33 initiated ivonescimab plus chemotherapy and comprised the overall treated cohort. Concurrent intrathecal or intraventricular chemotherapy was administered to 29 of 33 patients (87.9%). The median age was 61 years (IQR 56-62); 24 (72.7%) were female; 24 (72.7%) had baseline ECOG performance status of 2-3. The median number of prior therapy lines was 4 (IQR 3-6). At a median follow-up of 8.28 months, median OS was 8.54 months (95% CI 5.75-14.32), median LM-PFS was 6.54 months (95% CI 3.42-11.86), and median systemic PFS was 4.83 months (95% CI 2.79-7.56). Three-month treatment persistence was 64.4% (95% CI 44.9-78.6). Among 29 patients evaluable for LM response, 6 achieved a response, yielding an LM response rate of 20.7% (95% CI 8.0-39.7) and an LM disease control rate of 82.8% (95% CI 64.2-94.2). Among 31 patients with evaluable safety documentation, grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 14 (45.2%), most commonly hematologic toxicities. No permanent ivonescimab discontinuation due to toxicity was documented. CONCLUSIONS: This cohort provides real-world outcome data for patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC and LM receiving multimodality salvage treatment incorporating ivonescimab plus chemotherapy after dose-escalated third-generation EGFR-TKI failure.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The growing threat to health systems posed by extreme weather events (EWEs) disproportionately affects people living with HIV and tuberculosis disease in high-burden, low-resource settings. In Zimbabwe, for example, the 2023-24 El Niño-induced drought intensified food insecurity and reduced access to clinics and medication for such vulnerable populations. We aimed to conduct a formative evaluation to assess the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery and identify potential climate-adaptive health-service strategies. METHODS: In this survey-based multicentre cross-sectional observational study with a formative evaluation supplemented by qualitative data, we surveyed people living with HIV from Sept 19 to Dec 19, 2024, across 321 clinics in Zimbabwe to describe their perceived impact of EWEs on their health. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. The inclusion criteria were being diagnosed with HIV, being older than 18 years, and receiving HIV care at Organization for Public Health Interventions and Development (OPHID) clinics during the study period. Individuals who were not receiving HIV care at an OPHID clinic or who were younger than 18 years were excluded. A client satisfaction survey was used to collect data from in-person surveys. The survey included questions related to the general effects of EWEs, such as drought, extreme heat, and flooding; how EWEs had affected HIV or tuberculosis care; and what, if any, services were currently available or should be made available to mitigate climate impacts on health. We also conducted six focus group discussions (FGDs; five to eight participants per group) between March 12 and May 12, 2024, across the Bulilima, Mangwe, and Matobo districts. We used a convenience sampling approach to select patients who had visited the health facility for medical check-ups, medication resupply, or viral load testing, as recorded in clinical registers and verified by clinical staff. Eligible participants for the FGDs were adults (≥18 years) with HIV, or with current or previous tuberculosis treatment, receiving care at the study facility during the recruitment period; those under 18 years or not receiving care at the facility were excluded. Participants' sex was self-reported at enrolment. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, whereas FGD data were analysed using a modified framework approach. The main outcomes were the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery outcomes, as reported by affected communities, and community-prioritised mitigation strategies to feasibly address climate-sensitive determinants and barriers to care. FINDINGS: Among 1804 eligible participants approached across 15 districts, all completed the survey and were included in the analysis. Most survey participants (1363 [75·6%] of 1804 participants) reported noticing changes in climate over the past 5 years; of these 1363 participants, 900 (66·0%) were female and 1024 (75·1%) participants reported disruptions to their HIV care during the time they noticed changes in climate. Survey respondents reported that climate-related disruptions were associated with increased food insecurity (reported by 877 [85·6%] of 1024 participants) and water shortage (667 [65·1%] of 1024 participants). Qualitative analysis confirmed that the barriers to HIV and tuberculosis care from EWEs included widespread food insecurity, crop failures, and livestock deaths, with consequent effects on income leading to challenges in paying for food and transportation to clinics. Participants highlighted the need for expanded services that facilitate social and economic wellbeing, including nutrition support, water access, transportation, and income-generating activities, and decentralised models of health-care delivery. INTERPRETATION: Extreme heat and drought affect food and water security and have financial implications, creating challenges for patients to access care in Zimbabwe. Our findings underscore the urgent need for integrated, climate-adaptive strategies to maintain HIV and tuberculosis care in such climate-vulnerable regions. papers.abstract_en: Metastasis is the primary cause of mortality in cancer including lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Preferentially expressed antigen of melanoma (PRAME), a cancer-testis antigen, displays context-dependent functions across malignancies, but its biological role in LUAD metastasis has not been clearly defined. Here, we demonstrate that the significantly upregulated PRAME in metastatic LUAD directly interacts with the m6A methyltransferase METTL3 and promotes its K63-linked non-proteolytic ubiquitination. This modification occurs at lysine 235 of METTL3, increases its protein stability and facilitates METTL3 interaction with METTL14 and WTAP. Consequently, m6A modification of TGFB2 mRNA and activation of the TGF-β signaling pathway are enhanced, which is essential for PRAME-driven pro-metastatic effects both in vitro and in vivo. Clinically, PRAME expression positively correlates with METTL3 protein abundance and TGF-β pathway activation, and is robustly associated with poor clinical outcomes. Taken together, our findings identify K63-linked ubiquitination as a previously unrecognized post-translational modification of METTL3 and underscore the importance of the PRAME/METTL3/TGF-β axis in LUAD metastasis, providing mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for this malignancy.

This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of NSCLC-to-SCLC transformation, covering the classification of NSCLC subtypes, advances in targeted therapy for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant lung adenocarcinoma, clinical manifestations of SCLC transformation, diagnostic technologies, therapeutic strategies, ongoing controversies, and future perspectives. papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To explore needs among persons with advanced COPD and informal caregivers, and to explore how palliative care can address those needs. BACKGROUND: COPD is a common, progressive disease affecting lung function and represents a leading cause of death. Advanced COPD is associated with a high symptom burden and poor quality of life. Persons with advanced COPD may benefit from palliative care, but its use among persons with COPD remains limited, also in Germany. METHODS: A qualitative, multi-perspective interview study was conducted with persons suffering from advanced COPD, informal caregivers, and formal caregivers (general practitioners, pulmonologists, and palliative care physicians). A total of 53 interviews were analysed following structuring (Kuckartz') as well as latent content analysis methods using MAXQDA. RESULTS: Key needs were identified in the following domains (1) management of dyspnoea and anxiety, (2) home-based healthcare, (3) emergency planning and support, (4) psychosocial care, (5) organisational support, and (6) timely information about COPD and palliative care. Persons who had previously received PC reported various needs met in the first five areas. CONCLUSIONS: Persons with advanced COPD and their informal caregivers reported numerous needs. Persons receiving palliative care reported relief from various needs. Timely information about COPD's progression and palliative care could increase acceptance and thus use of palliative care among these persons and could consequently reduce or curtail the burden of living with advanced COPD.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: Using more than five decades of national data, we examine how age, period and cohort factors influence lung cancer mortality in Switzerland, and forecast future death counts to the early 2040s. METHODS: Lung cancer deaths were extracted from Swiss vital statistics. We applied age-period-cohort (APC) modelling to lung cancer mortality rates using substantiated assumptions about the age-mortality relationship as model constraints. To account for the uncertainty in the age-mortality relationship, boundary constraints were applied to the line of APC solutions, yielding a range of plausible results. In an alternative model, we replaced the cohort terms with smoking prevalence estimates from Swiss health surveys, enabling unconstrained modelling of age and period effects. Predictions are based on modelled age trends, and linearly extrapolated period and cohort trends. RESULTS: Plausible age, period and cohort effects indicated that age-specific mortality risks decline at the oldest ages, that period effects were minimal, while cohort effects showed distinct peak risks for men born around 1909 and women born around 1954. Among women, birth cohorts with the highest mortality closely aligned with those exhibiting the highest smoking prevalence. The models predicted a decline in the number of lung cancer deaths among men beginning in the mid-2020s, and among women from the mid-2030s onwards. CONCLUSIONS: This population-based analysis of lung cancer mortality not only highlights declining mortality rates in men of all ages, but reveals an emerging downward trend among younger women. We predict that the total number of lung cancer deaths in women will begin to decrease by the mid-2030s.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) are associated with substantial short term mortality and healthcare utilization, yet the prognostic utility of the immunonutrition based hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score in this setting remains unclear, particularly in comparison with the well validated dyspnoea, eosinopenia, consolidation, acidaemia, atrial fibrillation (DECAF) score. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single centre observational cohort study of adults presenting to the emergency department (ED) with AECOPD between June 2022 and June 2025. DECAF and HALP scores were calculated at admission using routinely collected clinical and laboratory data, and the primary outcome was 30 day in hospital mortality. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with Youden-derived, data-driven cut-off values, and we further evaluated previously validated DECAF thresholds and a categorical DECAF model. Associations with 30 day mortality were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for baseline clinical variables. Model calibration was evaluated using Brier scores and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and 30 day survival was analysed with Kaplan-Meier. RESULTS: A total of 499 patients were included in the study, 63 (12.6%) died within 30 days, and 76% of the cohort were male. The HALP score showed acceptable predictive performance (area under the curve (AUC) 0.724), at a cut-off of 16.84, sensitivity was 57.1%, specificity 75.0% and negative predictive value (NPV) 92.4% for 30 day in hospital mortality. The DECAF score demonstrated excellent discrimination for 30 day in hospital mortality (AUC 0.932), and showed significantly better discrimination than HALP (DeLong p < 0.001), using a cut-off of ≥ 4, sensitivity was 76.2%, specificity 95.6% and NPV 96.5%. CONCLUSION: In ED patients with AECOPD, the HALP score provides only limited prognostic information for 30 day in hospital mortality, whereas the DECAF score exhibits excellent discriminative performance and retains its value as a robust, clinically applicable predictor of short term outcomes in acute care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is a substantial comorbidity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the neural mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. This study aimed to assess alterations in effective connectivity (EC) in patients with COPD and investigate their relationships with clinical measures. METHODS: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (RS-fMRI) was performed in 38 patients with COPD and 30 healthy controls. EC was estimated using vector autoregressive (VAR) modelling combined with Granger causality analysis across 26 prespecified brain regions of interest derived from our previous functional connectivity study of the same cohort. Between-group differences in directed connectivity were assessed using Welch's t-tests. Associations between EC measures showing between-group differences and clinical measures were evaluated using age-adjusted partial Pearson correlations. RESULTS: At the nominal two-sided p < 0.05 level, 37 directed connections showed between-group differences in effective connectivity, and the mean vector autoregressive coefficients for 35 of these connections lay on opposite sides of zero between the COPD and control groups. Among the connections showing between-group differences, age-adjusted associations in patients with COPD involved pulmonary function, systemic oxygenation, cognition, affect, and health status. These associations involved distributed cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions, with several directed connections showing convergence across multiple clinical domains. CONCLUSION: Resting-state VAR-based EC revealed distributed between-group differences in direction-sensitive BOLD temporal organization in COPD. Several of these EC measures were associated with pulmonary function, SpO2, respiratory and COPD symptom burden, cognition, affect, and health status after age adjustment. These findings extend the functional connectivity profile of COPD by linking directed temporal relationships to its multidimensional clinical burden.

papers.abstract_en: Benchmarks labelled by panels of human readers underpin most medical image analysis. We ask whether such a dataset has a single attainable ceiling. All 1319 annotation files of the Lung Image Database Consortium image collection (LIDC-IDRI) were parsed into 7034 reader-level ratings. Modelling each nodule by a latent malignancy propensity of which the four reader verdicts are conditionally independent draws, we prove that no image-based model can exceed, against a reader-derived label, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the propensity itself; we derive how that bound depends on the labelling policy, test the independence assumption against a prediction the fit does not use, simulate its failures, and audit a purposive sample of 22 published studies against the rules they declare. Among 905 nodules read by all four radiologists, all four agreed exactly for 11.7% and 58.0% carried ratings spanning two or more points. Across three latent families, retaining every nodule the ceiling is 0.898-0.913; discarding the 19.6% the readers split two-two lifts it to 0.946-0.954; retaining only unanimous nodules discards 57.7% and lifts it to 0.991-0.994. On the binary scale, no family predicted more reader agreement than observed; simulated reader heterogeneity would make these ceilings slightly low. Of 27 reported figures, 11 lie above the bound implied by the study's own declared rule, four beyond sampling error and two if modest heterogeneity is also allowed for. The ceiling is set by the label, not by the images.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Brain metastases (BM) are frequent in EGFR-mutated (EGFRm) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and remain challenging after prior EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. Patients received 160 mg firmonertinib once daily. The primary endpoint was intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS). Archival paired primary tumors and BM specimens from an independent retrospective cohort underwent exploratory digital spatial profiling (DSP). RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 19.7 months (95% CI, 14.5-25.3), median iPFS was 14.6 months (95% CI, 4.2-not estimable [NE]), with 12- and 18-month iPFS rates of 53.8% and 46.1%, respectively. Median systemic PFS was 10.7 months (95% CI, 3.9-NE). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 13 (56.5%) patients, mostly grade 1; one patient (4.3%) developed grade 3 stomatitis. No treatment discontinuations or treatment-related deaths were observed. L858R BM displayed tumor-intrinsic, microenvironment-independent biology, suggesting preferential sensitivity to high-dose firmonertinib.

While tobacco smoking is a well-established risk factor for lung cancer,the association between cannabis use and lung cancer risk remains unclear and controversial. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus to identify cohort and case-controlstudies up to September 2025. CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis indicates that marijuana smoking may increase lung cancer risk, with cohort studies showing asignificant twofold association. Although case-control studies were not statistically significant, the upward trend highlights theimportance of considering cannabis use in lung cancer risk assessments and patient counseling.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Entosis is an actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell process that may culminate in lysosome-mediated entotic cell death and is implicated in tumor evolution. Its clinical relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. METHODS: To construct an Entosis-related Prognostic Prediction Index (EPPI), this study integrated TCGA-LUAD transcriptomic, clinical, and somatic mutation data. Three independent GEO cohorts provided external validation. The initial candidate gene set covered components driving cell-in-cell formation and the intracellular degradation of internalized cells. For subgroup comparison, the analytical approach incorporated survival analysis, functional enrichment, tumor microenvironment profiling, mutation analysis, immunotherapy assessment, and drug-sensitivity prediction. Tissue and cellular distributions of the EPPI genes were mapped using spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing. Molecular docking assessed predicted drug-target interactions. Finally, in vitro RAC1 knockdown experiments evaluated the cellular function of a representative EPPI gene. RESULTS: Comprising RND3, RAC1, KRAS, CTNNA1, AURKA, and ACTB, the final EPPI consistently stratified overall survival across all cohorts and showed moderate prognostic discrimination. The high-EPPI group had greater tumor purity and mutational burden, with enhanced cell-cycle, DNA-repair, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and NF-κB programs, whereas the low-EPPI group showed greater immune and stromal infiltration. TIDE and immunophenoscores also differed between subgroups. Drug-response models predicted greater sensitivity to cisplatin and paclitaxel in the high-EPPI group and to several targeted agents in the low-EPPI group. Molecular docking predicted RAC1-EHT-1864 and AURKA-alisertib interactions. Spatial and single-cell analyses showed heterogeneous EPPI-gene expression, with ACTB and RAC1 broadly distributed and AURKA restricted to selected populations. RAC1 depletion suppressed LUAD-cell proliferation, DNA synthesis, migration, and invasion. CONCLUSION: The EPPI is an entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification in LUAD. Based on this index, patients can be separated into subgroups with distinct proliferative features, genomic alterations, tissue compositions, and predicted drug sensitivities. These findings associate entosis-related molecular features with distinct cellular and clinical characteristics of LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: Acquired resistance to osimertinib remains a critical clinical challenge in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with 40%-60% of progressing patients lacking an identifiable genetic resistance driver. Through quantitative secretomic profiling of paired osimertinib-sensitive and -resistant NSCLC cell lines, we identified laminin subunit γ2 (LAMC2) as markedly enriched in resistant cell secretomes. Single-cell RNA sequencing reanalysis revealed a LAMC2-high drug-tolerant persister subpopulation that expanded under osimertinib pressure, with pseudotime analysis suggesting progressive co-upregulation of LAMC2 and matrix metalloproteinase 14 (MMP14) along the treatment-to-resistance trajectory. Across four independent cohorts, MMP14 exhibited the strongest co-expression with LAMC2 among all metalloproteinases; the two proteins also physically interacted, and their concurrent high expression predicted the worst overall survival. Mechanistically, MMP14 cleaved LAMC2 to release a bioactive Domain III (DIII) fragment harboring EGF-like repeats, which reactivated EGFR/AKT/ERK signaling despite continued osimertinib exposure. Exogenous DIII conferred resistance in sensitive cells, whereas an anti-DIII blocking antibody reversed MMP14-driven resistance in cell lines and patient-derived organoids. The selective MMP14 inhibitor NSC405020 restored osimertinib sensitivity in vitro and suppressed xenograft growth. In residual tumor tissues from neoadjuvant osimertinib-treated patients, non-responders exhibited higher LAMC2/MMP14 co-expression and more prominent spatial exclusion of CD8⁺ T-cells from the tumor core compared with major pathological responders. These findings identify the MMP14-LAMC2-DIII proteolytic axis as a non-genetic resistance mechanism and suggest that MMP14 inhibition or DIII neutralization may represent a rational strategy to overcome acquired osimertinib resistance.

papers.abstract_en: Accumulating evidence has shown that the dysfunction of mitochondria, the multifunctional organelles in various cellular processes, is a pivotal event in the development of various diseases, including human cancers. The molecular alterations in tumors that promote metabolic diversity and distinct targetable dependencies remain poorly defined. The mitochondrial transporter SLC25A20, also known as carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase (CACT), is crucial for fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO) by importing acylcarnitines into the mitochondrial matrix. Here, we demonstrate that SLC25A20 is significantly upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) tissues and cells, and its expression correlates with poor patient survival. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments reveal that SLC25A20 promotes tumor cell proliferation, survival, migration, and invasion by enhancing FAO-associated mitochondrial bioenergetics and suppressing apoptosis. Mechanistically, SLC25A20-mediated FAO maintains mitochondrial function and supports oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), thereby sustaining tumor bioenergetics and redox homeostasis. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic silencing of SLC25A20 impairs tumor growth in vivo. These findings establish SLC25A20 as a key metabolic driver in LUAD and suggest it may be a therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_en: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a common severe complication of advanced lung cancer and significantly worsens prognosis. Physical targeted therapies, represented by piezocatalytic therapy, sonodynamic therapy, photodynamic therapy, hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy, radiofrequency ablation and thermosensitive in situ hydrogel drug delivery system, induce reactive oxygen species generation via light, ultrasound, or piezocatalytic energy, or achieve tumor killing through local hyperthermia and temperature-controlled drug release, offering new strategies for MPE. papers.abstract_en: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) have advanced the study of complex lung diseases by resolving cellular heterogeneity, tissue architecture, and intercellular communication. These technologies are particularly informative in chronic respiratory disorders, where pathological remodeling involves coordinated alterations across epithelial, stromal, immune, and endothelial compartments. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a rare fatal fibrotic disorder, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a prevalent heterogeneous respiratory condition, represent distinct chronic lung diseases shaped by persistent injury, maladaptive repair, and progressive tissue remodeling. However, current understanding of their pathogenesis remains incomplete, and conventional approaches lack the resolution to define disease-associated cell states, spatially restricted niches, or compartment-specific interactions. This review synthesizes recent scRNA-seq and ST studies in IPF and COPD, emphasizing how high-resolution atlases refine established pathobiological frameworks and reveal shared and disease-specific cellular programs. We further discuss stromal and immune remodeling, hypoxia-associated vascular remodeling, and the translational implications of these findings for molecular stratification, target prioritization, and mechanism-informed therapeutic development, while noting limitations related to end-stage tissue sampling, platform constraints, and mouse-human correspondence. This review provides an integrated framework for understanding the cellular and spatial mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis and translational relevance of IPF and COPD.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous disease with distinct inflammatory profiles that may be associated with key pathological features, including emphysema and airway wall remodeling. Cluster 4 (Extremely high inflammation) was characterized by markedly elevated levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, intermediate symptom burden, relatively preserved pulmonary function, pronounced airway wall thickening and a high frequency of moderate-to-severe exacerbations. CONCLUSION: Integrating cytokine profiles with airflow limitation identified four exploratory COPD phenotypes, highlighting a potential dissociation between systemic inflammation and disease severity. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Smoking has been linked to alterations in plasma protein profiles and increased risk of esophageal cancer (EC). However, the precise mediating roles of plasma proteins in this relationship remain unclear. This study explores the mediation effects of plasma proteins in smoking-associated EC, utilizing genetic proxies to uncover potential biological mechanisms underpinning this association. METHODS: Genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were applied to examine the association between smoking traits and EC. Pathway enrichment analysis explored circulatory protein changes in smokers. A two-step mediation MR analysis identified key plasma proteins involved in smoking-related EC pathogenesis. Survival analysis assessed the impact of transcriptional levels of mediators on EC prognosis, while phenome-wide association studies (PheWAS) evaluated the safety of targeted molecules and investigated potential pleiotropy. The expression and function of ADH7 were evaluated by qRT-PCR and in vitro experiments. RESULTS: Genetic correlation analysis showed significant links between smoking and EC, supported by MR findings that confirmed a causal relationship. Smoking was found to influence pathways related to cytokine signaling, immune activation, and the STAT pathway. Five plasma proteins (ADH7, CPXM1, FUT3, GZMM, LYPD3) were identified as mediators in smoking-driven EC risk. Among these, ADH7 emerged as a key protein and was consistently associated with smoking traits; high ADH7 mRNA expression in EC tumor tissue was associated with reduced progression-free survival. PheWAS inferred that ADH7-targeted interventions might pose risks of neurological or psychiatric side effects, though these were not statistically significant. qRT-PCR and immunohistochemistry showed that ADH7 was downregulated in EC tissues relative to adjacent normal mucosa, and functional assays demonstrated that overexpression of ADH7 suppressed the proliferative and migratory capacity of EC cells. Serum ELISA further revealed that circulating ADH7 concentrations were elevated in smokers and in EC patients, with the highest levels observed in smoking EC patients, supporting a role for smoking-driven elevation of circulating ADH7 in EC risk. CONCLUSIONS: This study reveals a compartment-specific, dual role for ADH7 in smoking-related EC: elevated circulating ADH7, driven in part by smoking, is associated with increased EC risk, whereas ADH7 acts as a tumor suppressor within esophageal tumor tissue. These findings provide novel genetic and mechanistic insights into smoking-related EC pathogenesis and highlight the importance of distinguishing circulating from tissue-level protein function when interpreting biomarker-disease associations.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To determine preliminary quantitative ADC thresholds for functional response and to evaluate whether integrating DWI metrics with RECIST 1.1 provides complementary information for early systemic therapy response assessment in bone metastases. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included lung cancer patients with pelvic bone metastases who underwent three MRIs between November 2015 and November 2023: baseline, early time point (<4 months, TP1), and late (6-15 months, TP2) time points. ROC analysis based on lesion size change at TP2 determined ADC thresholds defining DWI response. A DWI response was defined as ADC >1300 µm²/s or ΔADC >0.14. An integrated response scheme (DWI-RECIST) combined this DWI-based response with RECIST assessment. Early responses at TP1 were compared between RECIST and DWI-RECIST using RECIST at TP2 as reference standard. Interobserver agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using net reclassification improvement and AUCs. RESULTS: Seventy-eight lesions from 27 patients were included. Compared with RECIST, DWI-RECIST yielded net classification gains of 7.4% (reader 1) and 11.1% (reader 2). DWI-RECIST showed higher AUCs than RECIST (reader 1: 0.6964 vs. 0.6184, p = 0.472; reader 2: 0.6415 vs. 0.6184, p = 0.781). Interobserver agreement for ADC was good (ICC 0.83-0.86). CONCLUSIONS: Integrating ADC-derived DWI metrics with RECIST 1.1 may provide complementary information for early assessment of pelvic bone metastases from lung cancer, particularly in lesions categorised as stable disease. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This pilot study proposes quantitative ADC thresholds and introduces a framework integrating these with RECIST 1.1 to support more objective response assessment in lung cancer pelvic bone metastases.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Black and Hispanic people with cystic fibrosis (PwCF) experience worse health outcomes. Health disparities are exacerbated by clinical research that does not adequately represent the diversity of the CF population. RESEARCH QUESTIONS: How do Black/African American and Hispanic/Latino(a) PwCF perceive clinical research? What are the barriers and facilitators to participation in research? Are there viable solutions to improve inclusion? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Semi-structured, individual interviews were conducted with PwCF aged ≥18 years who identify as Black/African American race and/or Hispanic/Latino(a) ethnicity. Participants were recruited from six geographically diverse CF centers and through CF Foundation Community Voice, a CF community partner organization. The interview guide was created by a committee that included minoritized PwCF, research coordinators, and physician-scientists. Thematic analysis with inductive and deductive coding was used to analyze interview transcripts. RESULTS: Twenty PwCF were interviewed from 2024 to 2025. Drawing from a race-conscious adaptation of the Behavioral Model for Vulnerable Populations, we used domains of predisposing, need-based, and healthcare environment factors, as well as emergent themes relating to information and support needs. Participants discussed barriers to research participation that included narrow eligibility criteria (e.g., genotype requirements, health status) and logistical challenges such as time and cost. PwCF described a sense of isolation as persons of color with CF, which impacted sense of trust in CF care and research studies. They highlighted that racialized experiences, especially doubt surrounding their CF diagnosis, significantly impact willingness to participate. Solutions center around providing community support to address feelings of isolation and information needs to provide transparency about study design and intent. INTERPRETATION: Participation in clinical research is strongly influenced by an interplay of social, cultural, health, and systemic factors. Solutions to improve inclusion in trials center the needs of marginalized communities across all phases of study design and implementation.

papers.abstract_en: Enteric‑type thymic adenocarcinoma (ETAC) is a rare subtype of thymic carcinoma. It shares highly similar histological and immunophenotypic features with intestinal adenocarcinoma, and is therefore prone to being misdiagnosed as metastatic carcinoma of gastrointestinal origin. Herein, we report a case of advanced ETAC with axillary lymph node oligometastasis. Positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) and gastrointestinal endoscopy were performed to rule out primary gastrointestinal malignancy. The patient underwent median sternotomy with extended thymectomy, which effectively relieved superior vena cava obstruction and cardiopulmonary compressive symptoms. Postoperatively, systemic chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy, as well as regional radiotherapy targeting the primary tumor bed and metastatic lymph nodes, were administered. The patient remained disease‑free during the 24‑month postoperative follow‑up. This case suggests that aggressive local therapy combined with molecular‑subtype‑based systemic treatment may offer novel therapeutic opportunities for carefully selected patients with advanced ETAC and oligometastases. .

papers.abstract_en: Atomically precise metal clusters hold great promise for cancer theranostics, yet current strategies for introducing tumor-targeting functionality often compromise their structural precision. Herein, an erlotinib (Er)-functionalized gold cluster, Au8-Er, is constructed through ligand engineering for targeted non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) theranostics. The Er ligands endow Au8-Er with high affinity toward the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), enabling selective tumor targeting and preferential accumulation at lung tumor sites. Under the glutathione-rich tumor microenvironment, Au8-Er releases Er to achieve chemotherapy. Simultaneously, the cluster exhibits strong X-ray attenuation and oxygen-sensitive phosphorescence, allowing it to function as both an X-ray scintillator and a photosensitizer for efficient X-ray-induced photodynamic therapy (X-PDT) under low-dose irradiation. Moreover, its X-ray-excited luminescence enables high-contrast imaging. The synergistic integration of targeted chemotherapy, X-PDT, and imaging within a structurally precise nanoplatform results in enhanced therapeutic efficacy against NSCLC. This work highlights ligand engineering as an effective strategy for imparting biological functionality to atomically precise metal clusters and advances their application in precision cancer theranostics.

papers.abstract_en: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic lung disorder strongly mediated by genetic susceptibility and aberrant epithelial repair mechanisms. Among the identified genetic factors, the MUC5B promoter polymorphism rs35705950 represents the most significant and frequently replicated risk variant associated with both familial and sporadic IPF. This review focuses on the mechanistic role of MUC5B dysregulation in promoting epithelial dysfunction and profibrotic signalling, with particular emphasis on its interaction with transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signalling and KL-6-associated epithelial injury. Excessive MUC5B expression within distal airways disrupts mucociliary homeostasis, prolongs epithelial exposure to inhaled toxic stimuli, and enhances persistent alveolar stress, thereby facilitating chronic epithelial injury and aberrant tissue repair. Sustained epithelial damage subsequently activates TGF-β-mediated SMAD signalling pathways, promoting fibroblast activation, myofibroblast differentiation, and extracellular matrix deposition. Emerging evidence further suggests a close relationship between MUC5B-associated epithelial dysfunction and elevated KL-6 expression, indicating that KL-6 may function as a downstream biomarker indicating ongoing epithelial injury and fibrotic progression. The proposed MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6 mechanistic signaling provides an integrated molecular network linking genetic susceptibility, epithelial dysfunction, biomarker elevation, and progressive fibrosis in IPF. In addition, telomere-related and surfactant-associated gene mutations further lead to epithelial instability and impaired regenerative capacity. Together, these interconnected molecular mechanisms provide significant insights into IPF progression and may support the development of biomarker-driven prognostic approaches and targeted precision therapies for improved disease management.

papers.abstract_en: Respirable crystalline silica (RCS) is a major occupational health hazard associated with silicosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), lung cancer, autoimmune diseases, and other systemic disorders. Saudi Arabia is undergoing rapid industrial expansion in sectors with substantial potential for RCS exposure, including mining, construction, cement production, glass manufacturing, oil and gas, engineered stone fabrication, and photovoltaic manufacturing. This review evaluates the potential risk of occupational RCS exposure in Saudi Arabia by integrating evidence from the scientific literature, government reports, labor and mining statistics, mineralogical data, and regulatory documents. The novel silica Hazard triangle framework was applied to assess three principal determinants of occupational exposure: workforce distribution, silica-containing materials, and high-risk industrial activities. Saudi Arabia possesses extensive reserves of high-purity silica sand, and continued expansion of mining and downstream silica-based industries may increase occupational exposure potential. The kingdom's arid climate may also contribute to dust generation and increase the occupational exposure of RCS. Although documented cases of silicosis confirm that silica-related disease exists in Saudi Arabia, published evidence on occupational exposure assessment, epidemiology, and health surveillance remains limited. International regulatory developments demonstrate the importance of health-based occupational exposure limits (OELs), exposure monitoring, engineering controls, and medical surveillance. Current Saudi labor law, National Council for occupational safety and health (NCOSH) policies, and General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) occupational disease frameworks provide an important legal and institutional foundation for the future development of silica-specific occupational health regulations. This review identifies important knowledge gaps and highlights the need for comprehensive exposure assessment, strengthened industrial hygiene capacity, and evidence-based regulatory strategies to reduce the future burden of silica-related diseases while supporting sustainable industrial development in Saudi Arabia.
